description: SPEC-021: an account-sheet line can reach its own entry and name the other side of it. Reported by an embedding app (its F-31) while making the account sheet answer the question it raises on every line — *6000 in debit, against what?* Before this, the route from a line to its entry was `journal` with fromDate and toDate on the same day and a filter by sequenceNumber: a search where a lookup belongs, for an entry whose identity the caller had two fields ago. The second step drives why `contraAccounts` is a LIST: the plain expense entry has exactly one counter account, the entry with input tax has two, and a field called "the counter account" would have to pick one and thereby invent a fact. Sorted by account number and deduplicated, so the same call comes back byte-identical. The bank sheet is the reverse view of the same two entries — on a credit line the DEBIT accounts answer the question, which is why the contra accounts are decided per line rather than per sheet.

steps.comment: A plain entry: one counter account.
A split entry: the expense line now has TWO accounts on the other side.

lines.comment: the input-tax line is on the SAME side as this one and is therefore not a counter account

projections.comment: The same two entries from the bank's side: now the debit accounts answer the question, and the split entry names both.
projections.name: accountSheet
